questions.prompt_en: The diagram describes a six-stage process for publishing a local news report: receiving a tip, checking sources, interviewing witnesses, drafting the report, editing and fact-checking, and publishing online. Summarise the process. Write at least 150 words.
questions.prompt_vi: Use present simple passive and accurate six-stage sequencing.

answer.model_en:
The diagram illustrates how a local news story is prepared and published online. The process consists of six stages, beginning with the receipt of information and ending with the release of the completed report.

Overall, the main feature of the process is that a story is checked several times before the public can read it. Information is first collected, then developed into a written article, and finally reviewed and published.

At the first stage, a news tip is received by the editorial team. The initial sources are then checked to establish whether the information is reliable enough to investigate. Next, witnesses are interviewed so that the reporter can obtain further details and compare different accounts of the event.

Once the necessary information has been gathered, a first draft is prepared. This draft is then edited for clarity and checked for factual accuracy. Any unclear claims need to be addressed before the final stage. After these checks have been completed, the report is published on the news website, where readers can access it.
